name: New Lanark
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: New Lanark is a former cotton-mill village tucked into the Clyde valley near Lanark, about 25 miles southeast of Glasgow. Founded in 1785 to harness the river's waterfalls, it became famous when Robert Owen ran it as a model community with good housing and a school. The mills spun cotton until 1968, and the restored stone buildings can now be explored.
